classification.difficultyReason: The student must step outside y=mx+c: read x=-3 from a vertical line, then explain that the gradient is undefined and y is not a function of x. Only one line is involved and little calculation is needed.

content.prompt: Here is the graph of a straight line.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write the equation of the line.

answer.worked: Every point on the line has $x$-coordinate $-3$, so the equation is $x=-3$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why the equation of this line cannot be written in the form $y=mx+c$.

answer.short: The line is vertical, so its gradient is undefined.
answer.worked: The line is vertical, so the run between any two points is $0$ and $\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}$ is undefined. There is no value of $m$, so the line cannot be written as $y=mx+c$.
